title: Why look for any judge other than Allah?
subtitle: The Book is detailed, and the decision is His

key.label: Where I go for the final word

then: The idolaters argued with the Prophet ﷺ and wanted their own standards to decide. He is told to say: {idea}shall I seek a judge other than Allah{/idea}, when He sent down the Book explained in detail? Ibn Kathir notes that people of earlier scripture {reward}knew it came from Allah in truth{/reward}, because their prophets had foretold him.
now: You disagree with your spouse and both of you start quoting podcasts, uncles, and online threads. {trap}Everyone is shopping for the judge who will side with them.{/trap} {idea}Start by asking what Allah actually said about it.{/idea}
old: I will keep asking around until someone tells me I am right.
new: Allah is the judge, and His Book is clear. I start there.
try: In your next disagreement, look up what the Quran says on the topic before arguing further.

title: His word is complete: true in news, just in command.
subtitle: No one can change what Allah has said
then: Qatadah explained it: {idea}true in what He stated, just in what He decided.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that everything Allah forbids brings harm, and {reward}none can turn back His judgment{/reward} in this life or the next. He hears what His servants say and knows what they do.
now: News apps update every ten minutes. Last year's advice is this year's mistake. Your boss rewrites the policy again. {reward}Allah's word does not get patched.{/reward} {idea}It was complete before you were born.{/idea}
old: Everything changes, so nothing can be relied on for good.
new: Allah's word is complete and true, and no one can change it.
try: Memorize this one short verse today and repeat it when the world feels unstable.

title: Follow the majority and they will lead you astray.
subtitle: Most people run on guesswork
then: In Makkah the believers were a small group surrounded by a large majority with old customs. Allah tells them {trap}if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they follow {trap}nothing but conjecture and wishful thinking{/trap}, and doubt their own way.
now: Everyone at work rounds up their timesheets. Everyone in the family takes the loan. Everyone at the party drinks. {idea}A lot of people doing something is not proof.{/idea} It is just a lot of people.
old: If most people do it, it cannot be that wrong.
new: The majority often runs on guesses. I follow what Allah made clear.
try: Pick one thing you do only because everyone does it. Ask honestly if Allah would approve.

title: Your Lord knows best who strays and who is guided.
subtitle: Leave the final sorting to Him

row.title: follow, and leave it to Him

then: Right after warning against following the guessing majority, Allah adds that {idea}He knows best who goes astray and who is guided.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says each one is made easy for what they were created for. The believers did not need to sort the people of Makkah themselves.
now: You see someone without hijab at the mosque, or a bearded man cutting in line, and your mind ranks them instantly. {trap}You have no access to their heart.{/trap} {idea}Allah knows who is guided. Your job is your own path.{/idea}
old: I can tell who is really guided by how they look.
new: Only my Lord knows who is truly guided. I focus on my own way.
try: Catch yourself judging someone's faith today. Replace the thought with a short dua for them.

title: Eat what Allah's name was spoken over.
subtitle: Food tied back to the One who provides it
then: Ibn Kathir says the pagans of Quraysh would eat {trap}what was sacrificed to idols{/trap}. Allah gives the believers permission to {idea}eat what His name was mentioned over{/idea}, tying their food back to Him. The verse links it to faith: if you believe in His signs.
now: Lunch at your desk, eyes on a screen, fork moving on autopilot. You do not even taste it. {idea}Saying Bismillah turns a meal back into a gift{/idea} from someone who chose to feed you today.
old: Eating is just something I do, it has nothing to do with Allah.
new: My food is His provision, and His name over it reminds me who gave it.
try: Say Bismillah out loud before every meal today, and pause one breath before the first bite.

title: He already told you what is forbidden. Why hold back the rest?
subtitle: Clear limits, mercy in need, and desires posing as knowledge
then: Some held back from food Allah had allowed while eating what He had forbidden, following pagan ideas. Allah says {idea}He has already explained in detail what is forbidden{/idea}, with room for real necessity. Then the warning: {trap}many lead others astray by their own desires, without knowledge.{/trap}
now: A relative insists something is haram because it feels wrong to them. Another declares something fine because they want it. {trap}Both are making rules from feelings.{/trap} {idea}Allah already made His limits clear. Learn them instead of guessing.{/idea}
old: What feels right or wrong to me is basically the same as what Allah wants.
new: Allah has explained His limits. My desires do not get to write new ones.
try: Think of one rule you follow or reject on feeling alone. Ask a qualified teacher about it this week.

title: Leave sin on the outside and sin on the inside.
subtitle: Public wrongs and hidden ones are both left behind
then: Mujahid and Qatadah said this covers {trap}all sins, public and secret, few or many.{/trap} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith of An-Nawwas: {idea}sin is what wavers in your chest and you hate for people to find out.{/idea} Every sin, seen or unseen, will be recompensed.
now: In public you are polite and careful. In your private browser history, or in the resentment you nurse quietly, it is a different story. {idea}The test is simple: would you be okay if this were seen?{/idea}
old: As long as my public life is clean, the rest is between me and nobody.
new: Allah asks me to leave the sins people see and the ones they never will.
try: Pick one hidden habit that makes your chest uneasy. Cut it back for just today.

title: Obeying others over Allah is a quiet kind of shirk.
subtitle: Devils feed arguments to their allies
then: Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi reported the idolaters' argument: {trap}you eat what you slaughter but not what Allah causes to die?{/trap} The verse says devils feed such arguments to their allies. Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}preferring anyone's word over Allah's law is shirk{/trap}, citing the hadith of Adi bin Hatim about obeying rabbis and monks.
now: A smart-sounding voice online twists a rule into a joke, and suddenly you feel silly following it. {trap}The argument is designed to sound clever.{/trap} {idea}The question is whose word you will follow.{/idea}
old: Shirk means worshipping statues. Following someone's opinion is just being open-minded.
new: When I put anyone's word above Allah's command, I give them a place that is His.
try: Notice one opinion you follow over a clear teaching. Ask yourself why it has that authority.

title: Once dead, then given life and a light to walk with.
subtitle: The believer who walks lit, and the one stuck in the dark
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a parable of the believer who was {trap}dead in confusion and misguidance{/trap}. Allah {reward}gave his heart life with faith{/reward} and a light to walk by among people. Ibn Abbas said the light is the Quran, As-Suddi said Islam. The other stays in layers of darkness he cannot leave.
now: You remember who you were before you started praying for real. Numb, scrolling, angry. {reward}Now there is a light you carry into the office, the kitchen, the hard conversation.{/reward} Do not forget you were once in the dark.
old: Faith is just one of many ways people choose to live.
new: Faith is the difference between being alive with a light and stuck in the dark.
try: Write one sentence about who you were before faith became real. Thank Allah for the change.

title: The great plotters only end up trapping themselves.
subtitle: Every town has powerful wrongdoers, and their plots turn back

row.title: the plot returns
sub: the good end is for the prophets

then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that the leaders opposing him in Makkah are not new. {trap}Every town had great ones among its wrongdoers who plotted{/trap}, and every prophet faced them. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}the good end was always for the messengers.{/reward} The harm of their plots and of misleading others falls on them.
now: Someone at work spins stories to push you out. It feels like they hold all the cards. {idea}Scheming has a way of collapsing on the schemer{/idea}, and they rarely see it coming. And check yourself too: are you plotting against anyone?
old: People who scheme and manipulate always come out on top.
new: Plots against the truth turn back on the plotter. I stay straight and patient.
try: If you are planning to get back at someone, drop the plan today and leave it to Allah.

title: They wanted to be prophets themselves. Allah knows whom to trust.
subtitle: Envy dressed up as a demand for proof
then: The leaders said they would not believe until {trap}they got what the messengers got.{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to their complaint that the Quran should have come to a great man of Makkah or Taif. They belittled the Prophet ﷺ out of envy, though they had called him Al-Amin. {idea}Allah knows best where to place His message.{/idea}
now: A younger colleague gets the promotion. A friend gets the blessing you prayed for. {trap}You start finding faults in them{/trap}, when the real feeling is: why not me? {idea}Allah knows who to trust with what.{/idea}
old: If someone gets what I wanted, they must not deserve it.
new: Allah knows best who to trust with each gift. Envy blinds me to it.
try: Congratulate, sincerely, one person who got something you wanted.

title: An open chest, or one that feels like climbing the sky.
subtitle: How guidance feels from the inside
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah {reward}opens the heart of the one He guides to Tawhid and faith{/reward}, making it easy. For the other, faith feels so heavy it is {trap}like trying to climb into the sky.{/trap} Sa'id bin Jubayr said Islam finds every path in that heart blocked.
now: Some days prayer feels like breathing out. Other days it feels like dragging yourself up a hill with no air. {idea}That feeling is worth noticing.{/idea} {reward}An open chest is something you can ask Allah for.{/reward}
old: If faith feels heavy, that is just how it is for me.
new: An open chest is a gift from Allah, and I can ask Him for it.
try: Say Rabbi ishrah li sadri, my Lord expand my chest, before your next prayer.

title: This is your Lord's path, and it runs straight.
subtitle: The signs laid out for those who take heed
then: After describing those who strayed and blocked others, Allah points to {idea}the path of your Lord, straight{/idea}, meaning Islam revealed through this Quran. Ibn Kathir says the signs are made clear {reward}for people of sound understanding{/reward} who take heed of what Allah and His Messenger convey.
now: Life feels like a maze of choices: which job, which city, which friends. {idea}The main road is not hidden.{/idea} Most of the twists come from looking away from it. The signs are clear to whoever stops and thinks.
old: The right path is confusing and hard to find.
new: My Lord's path is straight and clear when I take the time to reflect.
try: Before one decision today, ask: which choice keeps me on Allah's straight path?

title: At the end of the straight path: a Home of Peace.
subtitle: Paradise with their Lord, and Him as their protector

row.title: a safe path, a safe home

then: Ibn Kathir says Paradise is called {reward}the Home of Peace{/reward} because its people are safe, having walked the straight path of the prophets. {idea}Just as their way was free of wickedness, so is their home.{/idea} Allah is their Wali, their protector and helper, because of what they did.
now: You come home after a brutal day: traffic, an angry client, a sick kid. You just want one place with no stress. {reward}That longing is a small picture of the Home of Peace.{/reward} The road there is built from today's quiet choices.
old: Peace is something I will never really have.
new: A Home of Peace waits at the end of the straight path, and Allah is my protector on it.
try: Do one kind thing today that brings peace to someone else's home.
